# ABA PayWay — Telegram Questionnaire for @payway_Integration_AI_bot (2026-10-03)

**Status:** READY TO SEND — answers are captured in a FOLLOW-UP run.
**Target:** `@payway_Integration_AI_bot`, Telegram Desktop group **AGENT_test_Sohail** (must be the OPEN chat — see §5).
**Companion files:** `questions.json` (machine-readable mirror, regenerated by `node build-questions-json.mjs`), `answers/ANSWERS.md` (capture template).

## 1. What this is & design rules

A simplified, bot-ready questionnaire distilled from the three open-question registers. The
Telegram bot has **no knowledge of this project**, so every message is self-contained: it names
the API family, states what we observed in the sandbox, then asks short numbered sub-questions.

Sources consolidated (open items only; already-answered items excluded — §2):

- `.scratch/skills-audit/ABA-QUESTIONS-2026-09-05.md` (Q-A…Q-G)
- `audit-results/four-pillars/ABA-OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` (canonical register Q1–Q56 — append-only, never renumbered here)
- `docs/internal/INTEGRATION-GAPS-AND-ABA-QUESTIONS.md` (consolidation, 2026-09-12 relay impact, N1–N12)

Design rules:

1. **One Telegram message per question group** (`T-00`…`T-42`). At send time every message MUST be
   prefixed with exactly `hi @payway_Integration_AI_bot ` (trailing space). The prefix is NOT stored
   in the message texts below or in `questions.json`.
2. Each group = API family (first sentence) → sandbox observation (second) → numbered sub-questions.
3. Priorities: **P0** = blockers / decisions (send first) · **P1** = production-contract confirmations ·
   **P2** = policy / owner confirmations (send last, if session budget allows).
4. The canonical register stays untouched. After capture, propose append-only status updates there (user-gated).
5. Message texts are the fenced `text` blocks in §3 — copy them verbatim; `questions.json` is generated
   from this page, so the page is the single source of truth.

## 3. The questionnaire

### P0 — Blockers & integration decisions

#### T-00 — [P0] Context primer (register: none)

```text
Hello! We build developer tooling (an SDK and CLI) on top of the ABA PayWay payment gateway APIs. We work in the PayWay sandbox with merchant profile ec476910 and use these API families: 1) purchase/checkout under /api/payment-gateway/v1/payments/ (purchase, generate-qr, check-transaction, transaction-detail, transaction-list, refund, pre-auth complete/cancel, close-transaction); 2) Payment Link APIs (create/detail/void); 3) Credentials-on-File tokenization (link-account, link-card, charge with a token, renew/details/remove — v3 token management); 4) payout and beneficiary whitelist APIs; 5) exchange rate. Requests are HMAC-SHA512 signed with per-endpoint field orders. We will send a series of short numbered questions about production behavior and sandbox observations. Partial answers are fine — please answer what you know, say so when you don't, and point us to the exact public doc page whenever something is documented.
```

#### T-01 — [P0] Purchase API: duplicate tran_id (register: Q9.1, Q27; skills-audit Q-F)

```text
Question about the Purchase API (/api/payment-gateway/v1/payments/purchase) and duplicate transaction IDs (tran_id): in sandbox, creating a transaction with a tran_id that already exists silently succeeds (code 00 again), but the resulting KHQR cannot be paid — scanning says "Transaction not found". A hosted-page re-POST for a closed duplicate first says code 4 "Duplicated Transaction ID". Please: 1) Does PRODUCTION reject duplicate tran_ids per merchant, and with which exact error code? 2) Why does sandbox accept them if the QR is unpayable? 3) If the create response is lost (network drop), is retrying with the SAME tran_id safe in production, or must a new ID be generated?
```

#### T-02 — [P0] generate-qr: duplicate tran_id + lifetime bounds (register: Q10)

```text
Question about the QR-generation API (generate-qr / merchant-initiated QR): in sandbox the SAME tran_id was submitted twice with different amounts and both times code 00 returned with two live QR payloads. Also, a lifetime below exactly 180 seconds is rejected with HTTP 400 code "04", and values up to ~27 hours are accepted (docs say minimum 3 minutes, maximum 120 days). Please: 1) Is duplicate tran_id on generate-qr intentional? 2) What does production do on reuse — reject, overwrite, or allow two concurrent QRs — and with which code? 3) Are the lifetime bounds identical in production (minimum 3 minutes, maximum 120 days)?
```

#### T-03 — [P0] Query APIs: visibility delay (register: Q9.2–3)

```text
Question about how quickly newly created transactions appear in the query APIs: in sandbox, check-transaction sees a fresh transaction in under 1 second, while transaction-detail needs about 5 seconds. Please: 1) In production, what is the expected visibility delay for check-transaction and for transaction-detail after creation? 2) Is the difference between the two endpoints an architectural guarantee we can rely on when tuning a poller, or incidental?
```

#### T-04 — [P0] Close Transaction: production contract (register: Q4, Q28; skills-audit Q-G)

```text
Questions about the close-transaction API (closes an open transaction/QR): in sandbox, KHQR scans are refused after close ("transaction expired"), but a hosted CARD checkout session was still approved twice after a successful close, and no read API (check-transaction, transaction-detail) ever shows a CLOSED status. Also, closing a tran_id that never existed returns code 00 "Success!". Please: 1) In PRODUCTION, can a hosted-card session still pay after a successful close? 2) Is there any API way to see that a transaction was closed? 3) If a closed transaction is paid anyway, what is the final state — auto-reversal? Who refunds the customer? 4) Is the code-00 answer for a never-existing tran_id intentional idempotent behavior, and does production match it? 5) Should re-closing an already-closed transaction return 00 again or a dedicated code?
```

#### T-05 — [P0] Purchase KHQR: scan validity window (register: Q26; skills-audit Q-E)

```text
Question about KHQR created via the Purchase API (not offline KHQR): the QR payload contains no expiry timestamp, but scan validity seems much shorter than the transaction lifetime. In sandbox, a QR whose transaction had lifetime 1440 minutes was scan-refused "Transaction expired" at age 2h15m, while a seconds-old QR paid fine. Please: 1) What exactly governs how long a purchase-API KHQR stays scannable — a fixed window (what length?), the lifetime field (in which unit?), or a per-profile rule? 2) Should merchants always instruct customers to scan promptly even when a long lifetime was set? 3) Is the behavior the same in production?
```

#### T-06 — [P0] Callbacks: retry contract + citable doc (register: Q6.1, Q40)

```text
Questions about PayWay callbacks (notifications POSTed to the merchant server): we understand delivery is a single best-effort attempt with no guaranteed retry (about a 5-second window; a one-off ~10-second retry is sometimes observed but must not be designed for), and recovery is polling Check Transaction. Please: 1) Is there a published document (name, URL, version) that states this single-delivery contract? 2) In production, after a failed delivery (server down, non-200, timeout), is there ANY retry, and after how long? 3) Is polling Check Transaction the officially recommended recovery?
```

#### T-07 — [P0] Callbacks: signature, ACK and sample vectors per service (register: Q46)

```text
Questions about callback signatures and acknowledgement, per notification type (online checkout, online QR, signed printed-QR "Customer Module", unsigned offline KHQR, payment-link pushback, credentials-on-file token notification): 1) Is an HMAC signature always present for each type, and what is the exact canonical string that is signed (field order, encoding)? 2) What HTTP response does PayWay expect from the merchant server — status 200, any specific body like "RECEIVEOK", is 202 accepted, and what is the response timeout? 3) Please share approved sample callback payloads that include nested objects, null/boolean/Unicode values and unknown extra fields, so we can test signature verification and parsing. 4) If a signature is missing, should the merchant silently downgrade to unverified processing, or reject the delivery?
```

#### T-08 — [P0] CoF token callback: HMAC canonicalization (register: Q18.5)

```text
Question about the credentials-on-file token notification callback: it arrives as JSON with header "x-payway-topic: PaymentNotification" and body {request_id, payment_credential:{ctid, pwt, status, expired_at, token_flag, ...}}. Its "x-payway-hmac-sha512" header does NOT verify using the request-signing canonicalization (sorted keys concatenated), and 19 alternative orderings also failed. Please: 1) What is the exact canonicalization / field order of the HMAC plaintext on THIS callback? 2) Or does this callback use a different signature scheme (key, encoding)? Until we can verify the signature we authenticate link deliveries indirectly via get-token-details using the request_id.
```

#### T-09 — [P0] CoF: customer-initiated removal notification (register: Q18.6)

```text
Questions about credentials-on-file tokens removed by the customer in the ABA Mobile app: we captured ZERO callbacks when a customer unlinked two accounts (while link-approval callbacks worked fine on the same URL), and get-token-details keeps returning status=1 (active) for the removed tokens — charges only fail later with code 105. Please: 1) Does ANY notification exist for customer-initiated removal (per-request callback or profile-level webhook)? If yes, where is it configured? 2) Should get-token-details report removed tokens differently (e.g., status 0)? 3) What is the recommended way for merchants to detect removal proactively?
```

#### T-10 — [P0] Sandbox ec476910: enablement batch (register: Q22.1, Q41, Q43, Q19.1, Q24.1–2)

```text
Our sandbox merchant profile is ec476910. Several features answer profile-level blockers; could you check or enable them for this profile (or provide a pre-enabled test profile)? 1) Card tokenization: hosted link-card answers HTTP 403 code 104 "Merchant not enabled token flag" (the account-linking leg already works). 2) Merchant-initiated tokenization charge flags MITU_FLEX / MITU_FIX / MITR_FLEX answer 403 code 105 on charges with a valid active token (CITU_FLEX charges fine). 3) Payout: beneficiary add answers code 32 "Service is not enable", and payment-link create with payout answers "Payout accounts are not in whitelist". 4) get-transactions-by-mc-ref answers HTTP 404 with an empty body while sibling endpoints work (it worked in earlier tests) — is that a regression, profile gating, or retirement? 5) What is the procedure for a merchant to request these enablements in sandbox?
```

#### T-11 — [P0] Subscription hash order, doc fix, hash freeze, expire_in (register: Q22.2–3, Q12, Q42)

```text
Three related items: 1) Subscription purchase (purchase API with ctid + token_flag=CITR_FIX + frequency 1W/1M/2M): the published docs list a 26-field HMAC order WITHOUT ctid, but the gateway enforces ctid signed between items and shipping (27 fields), and the "Wrong Hash" error hint prints the documented (wrong) list. Please confirm the authoritative field order and fix the docs page and the error hint. 2) Are the published per-endpoint HMAC field orders now frozen, and how would future changes be announced (changelog, spec version)? Do the same orders apply unchanged in PRODUCTION? 3) On the account-linking response, expire_in arrives as an absolute epoch-seconds timestamp equal to creation + ~90 seconds, while the docs say "10 minutes". Please confirm expire_in is the epoch instant of the link-QR expiry and what the intended validity window is.
```

#### T-12 — [P0] Production base URL + UAT environment (register: Q16)

```text
Two questions about PayWay environments: 1) Please confirm the PRODUCTION base URL is https://checkout.payway.com.kh and that all current endpoint paths exist identically there, including the -2 suffixed versions and the v3 token-management paths. 2) Is there a separate UAT or certification environment between sandbox and production, with its own base URL?
```

```text
Questions about credentials-on-file token expiry (tokens expire after about 90 days): 1) Is validity exactly 90 calendar days from grant/renewal, or rolling/usage-based? 2) Which timezone governs the boundary day? 3) What error code does a charge return when the token is expired but not yet removed? (Charges on REMOVED tokens decline with code 105 — is expired the same or a different code?)
```

In sandbox, some probes accepted values outside the documented set (e.g., CITO_FIX, CITR_FLEX on certain calls) — are those sandbox-only, and should clients reject them? Also please confirm that CITR_FIX is intentionally invalid on the linking endpoints (linking uses CITI_FLEX / CITO_FLEX only).
```

```text

Our working numbers to confirm or correct: check-transaction 600/min, transaction-detail 10/min, transaction-list 50/min, refund 500 per second, get-transactions-by-mc-ref 10/min. Please: 1) Confirm or correct these for production. 2) Is standard HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header planned? 3) What is the penalty model — throttled per API key, per merchant profile, or per source IP — and how long does a block last? 4) What does the production 429 response body look like?
```

#### T-16 — [P1] Transaction list: unpaid QR visibility + window cap (register: Q11)

```text
Questions about the transaction list API: 1) In sandbox it returns only paid and checkout-created transactions — unpaid QR-only transactions never appear, although check-transaction sees them in under a second. Is that the intended production contract? 2) Is there a filter or variant that includes unpaid open QR transactions (needed to reconcile abandoned-but-still-scannable QRs)? 3) The date window is capped at 3 days ("Maximum date rang is allowed only 3 days") — is the cap the same in production, and can it be raised per merchant?

#### T-17 — [P1] get-transactions-by-mc-ref: canonical envelope (register: Q34, Q24.3)

```text

Please: 1) Which envelope is canonical in production, and will it stay stable? 2) Is the string "00" the success code in both sandbox and production? 3) Is this endpoint supported in production, and is the documented 10-per-minute throttle current?

```text
Questions about proving payments and recovering lost responses: 1) check-transaction responses do not include the original currency. For final proof of an approved payment, is there a recommended combination of the signed callback plus a current query that avoids extra transaction-detail calls (or must approval use paced transaction-detail requests)? 2) If a create/refund/capture/payout response was lost (network drop), what is the reliable recovery — query by tran_id, by merchant reference, or something else? 3) Can a QR or payment link genuinely be paid more than once (repeat payments)? What duplicate-payment identity rules apply per QR/link type? 4) What is the maximum historical window for the query APIs (7 days?), and does it differ per endpoint?

#### T-19 — [P1] Payment link: pushback parity + invalid-id code (register: Q20, Q21)

```text
Questions about Payment Link pushbacks (POST to the link's return_url): we captured {tran_id, status:0, merchant_ref_no} as application/json with NO hash field; status is numeric 0, while the official sample shows "status": "00". Please: 1) Does the production pushback also carry no HMAC/hash? 2) Can pushback status take values other than 0 (failed, cancelled?) and what do they mean? 3) Can more than one pushback arrive per payment? 4) For an invalid or unknown link id, the docs say PTL132 "Invalid payment link" but sandbox answers HTTP 403 code 96 "Invalid merchant data" — which code does production return?
```

#### T-20 — [P1] Payment link: lifecycle + datatype parity (register: Q33)

```text
Questions about Payment Link lifecycle and data types: 1) Is there a terminal EXPIRED status for payment links in production, or must merchants enforce expiry locally? (Sandbox: links past expired_date still read OPEN and the hosted page still answers HTTP 200.) 2) What are the canonical production types of tran_id, amount, total_refund and expired_date in create/detail responses and pushbacks? (Sandbox: tran_id numeric in create/detail but string in pushbacks; unset expired_date echoes the string "0"; create/detail disagree on total_refund.) 3) When is pushback_url present in the detail response, and when is it omitted? 4) What is the minimum future expired_date offset, and which error code applies for past or too-soon values? (Sandbox PTL04 seems to be a catch-all.) 5) Are PTL04, PTL05, PTL99 and PTL132 all active production codes, and which condition maps to each?
```

#### T-21 — [P1] Payment link: void endpoint parity (register: Q37)

```text
Questions about the payment-link void endpoint (POST /api/merchant-portal/merchant-access/payment-link/void — it has no published docs page). We mapped it on sandbox: RSA-encrypted merchant_auth {mc_id, id}, HMAC over request_time + merchant_id + merchant_auth; success answers {status:{code:"00"}, tran_id} with a numeric tran_id; the link then reads VOIDED in detail; the hosted page renders an invalid-data shell (code 07); a second void answers HTTP 403 PTL188 "The payment link is already voided.". Please: 1) Is void available in PRODUCTION with the same path, signing and responses, and is an official docs page planned? 2) Can a PAID or partially-paid multi-payment link be voided, or is it rejected — with which code? 3) Do in-flight payments on a link survive a void (does the pushback still fire, does check-transaction still approve)? 4) Is PTL188 final in production for a double void? 5) Should merchants refund paid links instead of voiding them?
```

```text
Question about merchant profile capabilities: for each payment method (ABA PAY, KHQR, cards incl. UnionPay/JCB/UPI, Alipay, WeChat, Google Pay), is there a versioned schema, API or portal view that tells a merchant WHICH methods, currencies, and capabilities (refund, pre-auth, tokenization) are enabled on THEIR profile? How can enablement be verified programmatically instead of inferring it from logos, enum values, or error codes?
```

#### T-38 — [P2] Go-live acceptance rule (register: Q44)

```text
Questions about production go-live acceptance for a new merchant: 1) What is the current acceptance rule — required transaction counts, amount caps, and required test cases per payment method/scheme/issuer? 2) Which cases are mandatory (refund, capture, credentials-on-file, payout)? 3) Can restricted customer traffic begin before the first settlement verification, and under what documented conditions?
```

#### T-39 — [P2] Settlement report sources + joins (register: Q45, N4 remainder)

```text
Questions about settlement reconciliation sources: 1) Which exact portal reports and bank statements do merchants join for reconciliation, with which fields and grain? 2) How do order IDs (APV) in the portal export join to aggregated bank bookings, and where are fees, refunds, FX, reserves and taxes shown? 3) How are later-batch adjustments and cut-offs/holidays handled, and what tolerance applies before a mismatch must be escalated?
```

#### T-40 — [P2] Checkout UI spec version + review process (register: Q50 remainder)

```text
Questions about the default checkout UI requirements (we received design exports titled 2.11 via the integration team): 1) Which guideline version is current, what is its effective date, and where is the canonical public source? 2) What is the supported device/embedded-browser matrix — do Telegram in-app browsers, external browsers, and native wrappers have different header/navigation requirements? 3) How are the vendor logo, checkout theme and continuation label configured per profile, which locales/labels are supported, and is there a required method order/spacing/currency typography? 4) What is the screen-review process before production credentials — review channel, required screenshots/recordings, approver, durable sign-off artifact — and is re-review required after profile changes? 5) Is the bottom-sheet presentation available to all profiles, and what rules govern the hosted-QR response (expiry, entitlement)?
```

#### T-41 — [P2] Checkout UI asset redistribution (register: Q56 remainder)

```text
Question about redistributing checkout UI assets: may the checkout UI SVG assets, the composite payment-method logo strip, and the design exports (including third-party card-network marks) be redistributed inside a public SDK package? If yes, under which license, version and update terms, and what is the canonical download source? Supplying the files for an implementation review is not the same as permission to bundle them publicly.
```

#### T-42 — [P2] Adjacent products: plugins, POS, Mini Apps (register: Q55)

```text
Questions about adjacent PayWay products: 1) Which commerce-platform plugins (e.g., WooCommerce, Magento, Shopify or others) are officially supported, and which plugin versions/features/upgrade paths? 2) Is there an official POS/ECR hardware integration contract (transport/protocol/firmware)? 3) What are the rules for ABA Mini Apps (app/profile/environment/domain/method/return rules)? 4) Who owns each of these contracts, and is there separate UAT acceptance for them (ordinary PayWay sandbox checks cannot certify these products)?
```

## 5. Next-run posting protocol (Telegram Desktop)

1. Invoke the **`telegram-desktop-control`** skill and read its SKILL.md first (2026-10-03 upgraded
   version: `readChat` returns FULL message bodies; dynamic twin scan; `clearDraft`/`waitFor`/`closeSearch`).
2. Target chat: **AGENT_test_Sohail** — it must already be the OPEN chat in Telegram Desktop. Chat
   switching is NOT accessibility-reachable (single-column window; header search is chat-scoped). If a
   different chat is open, STOP and ask the user to open it.
3. **Prefix rule:** every message = exact prefix `hi @payway_Integration_AI_bot ` (trailing space) +
   the stored `text` from `questions.json`. Never omit or alter the prefix.
4. No synthetic keystrokes/mouse: submit text via the skill's batch send (`sendAll`); retrieve via
   `readChat` (full bodies land in the `text` field).
5. Order: T-00 primer → check for a reply → P0 (T-01…T-12) → P1 (T-13…T-35) → P2 (T-36…T-42).
   Send in batches of 3–5 messages; after each batch, wait for bot replies, capture (§6), then continue.
6. Skill traps to respect: disableDiffing before diffs; chat/element indices SHIFT on mutation (re-scan);
   clearDraft before typing; waitFor to confirm sends; closeSearch after any search; stale-guard retry on
   flaky sends; match the chat by the noisy-title contains-rule.
7. If the bot does not answer a group (after one polite nudge), record "no answer" on the status board
   and move on — do not spam retries.
8. Resume support: the status board in `answers/ANSWERS.md` tracks asked/answered per ID; a resumed run
   skips completed rows.
9. Provenance: any relayed-style answer must be captured with owner/date/environment scope before it is
   propagated anywhere (register rule for Q44–Q56 answers).

## 6. Answer capture format

All capture lands under `answers/`:

```
answers/
  ANSWERS.md            # status board + one section per T-id (template below)
  raw/T-01.md …         # VERBATIM bot replies per question (one file per ID)
```

Per-ID section template (append to `ANSWERS.md`):

```markdown
### T-01 — Purchase API: duplicate tran_id (register Q9.1, Q27)
- Asked at: <timestamp>
- Raw reply: answers/raw/T-01.md
- Extracted facts:
  1. <fact — one per line; keep numbers/codes verbatim>
- Confidence: high | medium | low — <why (bot certainty, doc reference given, etc.)>
- Proposed register update: <append-only proposal, e.g. "Q27.1 → answered (operationally, telegram relay 2026-10-XX)"> (user-gated, do NOT edit the register directly)
```

Rules: never paraphrase numbers/codes in "Extracted facts"; keep the raw reply verbatim in `raw/`;
mark unanswered groups "no answer" instead of deleting the section; at end of run, summarize counts
(answered / partial / no answer) at the top of `ANSWERS.md`.

## 7. Machine-readable mirror

`questions.json` mirrors §3 (id, priority, topic, register, text — without the Telegram prefix).
Regenerate after any edit to this page:

```
node build-questions-json.mjs
```
